definitions.explanation: An intelligent marine mammal known for its playful behavior, agility, and ability to be trained. Dolphins are popular attractions at aquariums in Japan.

examples.japanese: ⟦{水族館|すいぞくかん}→水族館：09220_suizokukan⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{海豚|いるか}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ショー→ショー：10950_shoo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: I watched a dolphin show at the aquarium.
Dolphins were swimming alongside the boat.

examples.japanese: {海豚|いるか}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{非常|ひじょう}→非常：01598_hijou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{知能|ちのう}→知能：03471_chinou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{知|し}られて→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Dolphins are known as highly intelligent animals.

notes:
{海豚|いるか} refers to dolphins. The kanji literally means "sea pig."

Alternative writing: ⟦イルカ→イルカ：noentry⟧ (katakana, common)

Common expressions:
- {海豚|いるか}⟦ショー→ショー：10950_shoo⟧ (dolphin show)
- {海豚|いるか}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{泳|およ}ぐ→泳ぐ：00545_oyogu⟧ (to swim with dolphins)
- ⟦バンドウ→バンドウ：noentry⟧{海豚|いるか} (bottlenose dolphin)

Counter: ⟦{頭|とう}→頭：18067_tou⟧ or ⟦{匹|ひき}→匹：00939_hiki⟧

Note:
Dolphins are distinct from ⟦{鯨|くじら}→鯨：04310_kujira⟧ (whales) though both are cetaceans. The smaller cetaceans are generally called {海豚|いるか}, while larger ones are ⟦{鯨|くじら}→鯨：04310_kujira⟧. ⟦{鼠海豚|ねずみいるか}→鼠海豚：noentry⟧ (porpoise) refers specifically to porpoises.
